title: Japan Turns to Heat-Resistant Rice as Climate Warms
paragraphs: As summers in Japan become hotter, more and more farmers are switching to types of rice that can tolerate high temperatures.

According to Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, heat-resistant rice varieties were planted on 248,000 hectares of land across Japan in 2025. This was an increase of 42,000 hectares compared with the previous year. As a result, a record 18.2% of the land used to grow the country's main type of rice was devoted to heat-resistant varieties. This share has nearly tripled over the past decade.

Heat-resistant rice was grown in 44 of Japan's 47 prefectures in 2025, with only Hokkaido, Iwate and Okinawa not growing it. Saga Prefecture, in southern Japan, had the highest share, with heat-resistant varieties making up 66.9% of its main rice crop. It was followed by Nagasaki, at 49.8%, and Shimane, at 47.3%. Meanwhile, in Kagoshima, the share quadrupled in just one year to 24.4%. The most widely planted heat-resistant variety was Kinumusume, followed by Tochiginohoshi and Koshiibuki.

The shift is a response to rising temperatures. In 2025, Japan experienced its hottest summer on record. When rice grains are exposed to high temperatures, they are more likely to crack during milling, which reduces the amount that can be sold as white rice. Heat damage has been partly blamed for the rice shortages that Japan has experienced in recent years. In addition, according to a government report, rice yields in Japan could fall by about 20% by the year 2100.
However, there are obstacles. Many of the heat-resistant rice brands are still not well known among consumers. In addition, some older farmers have been reluctant to change the varieties they grow.

According to Yuji Masutomi, an expert at the National Institute for Environmental Studies, more farmers should plant heat-resistant rice in the coming years. However, Masutomi warned that if consumers do not buy these varieties, farmers will be reluctant to grow them, so marketing is vital to encourage people to try them.
Scientists are also working on new solutions. For example, researchers have identified a gene that causes rice plants to flower earlier in the day, when temperatures are cooler.
